verses.text: This is what the LORD told Jeremiah.
“Stand at the gate of the LORD’s house and speak up right there. Say, ‘Everyone from Judah coming through these gates to worship the LORD, listen to what he says.’”
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Change how you live and what you do, and I’ll let you stay here.
Quit trusting the lies people keep repeating: ‘This is the LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple!’
If you really change how you live and what you do, and if you make sure people and their neighbors get a fair hearing,
if you stop mistreating foreigners, children without fathers, and widows, stop spilling innocent blood here, and stop chasing other gods to your own ruin,
then I’ll let you live right here in the land I gave your ancestors long ago to keep forever.
Look at you, trusting lies that won’t do you a bit of good.
Are you really going to steal, murder, cheat on your spouses, swear to lies, burn incense to Baal, and chase gods you’ve never known,
and then stand in front of me in the house that bears my name and say, ‘We’re safe now,’ just so you can go right back to doing those disgusting things?
Do you look at this house that bears my name and see a hideout for robbers? I’ve seen what’s going on myself,” says the LORD.
“Go on, then, to my place at Shiloh, where I first put my name. See what I did to it because of the evil my people Israel were doing.
You’ve done all those things,” says the LORD. “I got up early to speak to you, but you wouldn’t listen. I called you, but you didn’t answer.
So I’ll do to this house that bears my name, the house you’re counting on, and to the place I gave you and your ancestors, exactly what I did to Shiloh.
I’ll throw you out of my sight the way I threw out all your relatives, all the descendants of Ephraim.
“So don’t pray for these people. Don’t cry out or pray on their behalf or plead with me for them. I won’t listen to you.
Can’t you see what they’re doing in Judah’s towns and in Jerusalem’s streets?
The kids collect wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of the sky. They pour out drink offerings to other gods to make me angry.
But is it really me they’re provoking?” says the LORD. “Aren’t they doing it to themselves and bringing shame right to their own faces?”

So the Lord GOD says, “Watch. My anger and fury will pour out over this place, over people and animals, the trees in the fields, and what grows from the ground. It’ll burn, and nobody will put it out.”
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Go ahead and throw your burnt offerings in with your other sacrifices and eat the meat.
When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I didn’t speak to them or give them orders about burnt offerings or sacrifices.
Here’s what I told them to do: ‘Listen to me. I’ll be your God, and you’ll be my people. Follow the whole path I tell you to take so things go well for you.’
But they wouldn’t listen or even turn an ear my way. They followed their own plans and their stubborn, evil hearts. They went backward instead of forward.
From the day your ancestors left Egypt right up to today, I’ve sent you all my servants the prophets. Day after day I got up early and sent them.
Still, they wouldn’t listen to me or even lean in to hear. They stiffened their necks and did worse than their ancestors.
“You’ll tell them every word of this, but they won’t listen to you. You’ll call to them too, but they won’t answer.
So tell them, ‘This is the nation that wouldn’t listen to the LORD their God or take his correction. Truth is dead. You won’t hear it from their mouths.’
Cut off your hair and throw it away. Go up on the bare hills and cry out in grief. The LORD has rejected and walked away from the generation that brought his anger down.
“The people of Judah have done evil right in front of me,” says the LORD. “They put their disgusting things in the house that bears my name and made it unclean.
They built worship sites at Topheth, in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so they could burn their sons and daughters in the fire. I never told them to do that. It never even crossed my mind.

So look, the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when nobody will call it ‘Topheth’ or ‘the valley of the son of Hinnom’ anymore. They’ll call it ‘the valley of Slaughter.’ They’ll bury people in Topheth until there’s nowhere left to bury them.
The bodies of these people will be food for birds and wild animals. Nobody will scare them off.
Then I’ll silence the laughter and the shouts of joy in Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s streets. You won’t hear a bride or groom there. The land will become a wasteland.”
